lines: {A} does not move for a long moment. Then: "No. Not {B}. Not like this."
{A} is still holding onto {B} when the others pull them back.
{A}'s voice breaks. "I had their back. I had their back the whole time."
{A} goes quiet in a way that is worse than shouting. {B} was supposed to make it home.
{A} stares at the spot where {B} fell, like staring hard enough could undo it.
{A} exhales hard. "Damn it. Damn it, {B}."
{A} didn't see that coming. Nobody did.
{A} keeps glancing back at where {B} went down, like they might just get up.
{A} says {B}'s name once, quietly, like it needs saying out loud.
{A} grips their weapon tighter. It doesn't help. It's just something to do with their hands.
{A} logs the loss without much expression. {B} is gone. The mission isn't.
{A} takes a breath, files it away, and keeps moving.
"Another one down," {A} says, to no one in particular.
{A} doesn't know {B} well enough to grieve properly. That doesn't make it easy to watch.
{A} marks the loss and keeps their eyes on the perimeter. Someone has to.
{A} looks away. Whatever was unresolved between them just became permanent.
{A} doesn't know what to feel, which is its own kind of bad.
"We never got that sorted out," {A} mutters, mostly to themselves.
{A} stands over where {B} fell longer than they'd like anyone to notice.
{A} feels something they didn't expect to feel about {B} dying. They don't examine it too closely.
{A} doesn't say anything. The silence is its own kind of statement.
"Guess that's settled, then," {A} says, and immediately hates how it sounded out loud.
{A} expected to feel something closer to relief. They don't.
{A} looks at where {B} fell and finds, against every instinct, that they wish they hadn't.
{A} keeps their face flat. Whatever this was between them, it didn't deserve to end like this.
